heading_en: General Requirements for the Internal Model Approach
summary_ja: 内部モデル方式採用最終指定親会社が満たすべき、リスク管理体制・ストレス・テスト・検証・システム等に関する一般的要件を定める。
summary_en: Sets the general requirements for an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach, covering risk management, stress testing, validation, trading desk designation, internal management models and systems.
paragraphs: An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall satisfy all of the following requirements. (i) In the market risk management system, material risks held by the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. are comprehensively identified and taken into account to the extent possible. (ii) Sufficient personnel familiar with the use of sophisticated models are secured not only in the front office but also in the risk management function and the internal audit function and, as necessary, in the back office. (iii) Records showing the accuracy of the measurement of the market risk equivalent amount under the internal model approach are retained. (iv) Stress tests (meaning the stress tests prescribed in Article 251; the same applies in the following item) are conducted regularly, and the results of those stress tests are used for the following. (a) Discussions by the board of directors, etc. held at a frequency of at least once a month. (b) Assessment of capital adequacy. (c) Formulation of risk management policies by directors, etc. and setting of limits including position limits. (v) Where a vulnerability to a particular event is revealed by the conduct of stress tests, arrangements are in place to promptly take measures to address that vulnerability appropriately. (vi) A trading desk approved to use the internal model approach has passed the back-testing for each trading desk prescribed in Article 253-3 and the profit-and-loss attribution test prescribed in Article 253-4. (vii) Prior to approval of the internal model approach, the results of the enterprise-wide back-testing prescribed in Article 253-2 for twelve months are submitted. (viii) Prior to approval of the internal model approach, monitoring over a certain period and testing using actual trading data have been conducted. (ix) The scope of portfolios to which the internal model approach is applied shall be updated quarterly on the basis of the latest results of the risk factor modellability test, back-testing and the profit-and-loss attribution test for each trading desk. (x) The trading desks that use the internal model approach satisfy all of the following requirements. (a) The designation of trading desks that use the internal model approach satisfies all of the following requirements. (1) Trading desks that use the internal model approach and trading desks that do not are designated, and the basis for the designation is clarified in a document. (2) It is assessed quarterly that the total market risk equivalent amount of the trading desks that use the internal model approach is at least 10% of the market risk equivalent amount of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. as a whole. (3) A trading desk is not designated as not using the internal model approach on the ground that the market risk equivalent amount calculated by the standardized method is smaller than that calculated by the internal model approach. (4) A trading desk that was not made subject to the application for approval of the internal model approach when approval under Article 250 for use of the internal model approach was sought shall not be made subject to an application for approval of the internal model approach for one year from the date on which use of the internal model approach was most recently approved. (b) In calculating the market risk equivalent amount under the internal model approach, the following procedures are followed. (1) Risk factors that continuously satisfy the profit-and-loss attribution test for each trading desk are identified. (2) Each trading desk continuously satisfies the back-testing requirements prescribed in Article 253-2 and Article 253-3. (3) Back-testing and the profit-and-loss attribution test are conducted quarterly, and the classification of the trading desk in the back-testing and the profit-and-loss attribution test is updated. (4) The market risk equivalent amount for risk factors that satisfy the risk factor modellability test is calculated using expected shortfall. (5) The market risk equivalent amount for risk factors that do not satisfy the risk factor modellability test is calculated using stressed expected shortfall. (xi) A Market Risk Management Department has been established. (xii) The Market Risk Management Department prepares a daily report including the following items. (a) The status of each trader's positions. (b) The results obtained from the trading desk's risk management models and the analysis thereof (including analysis relating to the exposure measurements and their relationship to trading limits). (xiii) The Market Risk Management Department reports the status of market risk management to the board of directors, etc. (xiv) Directors, etc. receive daily reports from the Market Risk Management Department on the report prescribed in item (xii) and review it. (xv) The model validation unit (meaning a department or function that is independent of the department that designs and operates the internal model approach and to which persons with sufficient capability belong; the same applies in the following item and item (xxii)(a)) validates all models used in the internal model approach at the time of approval and thereafter at a frequency of at least once a year. (xvi) The model validation unit reports the results of the validation prescribed in the preceding item to the board of directors, etc. (xvii) The board of directors, etc. is actively involved in the management of market risk and allocates appropriate management resources. (xviii) The manager of the Market Risk Management Department has the authority to instruct the reduction of each trader's positions. (xix) Where the internal model approach differs from the models used in the internal management of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach (hereinafter referred to as the "internal management model"), all of the following requirements are satisfied. (a) The valuation models used in the internal model approach and the internal management model are as identical as possible. (b) The internal model approach and the internal management model are as identical as possible with respect to the identification, measurement, management and internal reporting of the price fluctuation risk of the trading desk. (c) The internal management model measures all positions subject to measurement of the market risk equivalent amount. (d) The identification of risk factors, estimation of parameters and design of proxies in the trading desk's risk management model are, in principle, carried out on the basis of the methods used in the internal management model. (e) The model used to calculate the market risk equivalent amount and the internal management model are, in principle, to cover the same risk factors. (xx) Documents on the operation, policies, management and procedures of the internal management model have been prepared, and arrangements are in place to comply with them. (xxi) Arrangements are put in place to accurately report numerical values based on appropriate theory and calculation for all models used to calculate the market risk equivalent amount under the internal model approach, the standardized method or the simplified method. (xxii) The systems relating to market risk measurement, including the internal model approach, satisfy all of the following requirements. (a) They are validated at a frequency of at least once a year by either the internal audit function and the model validation unit, or an external auditor. (b) The validation under (a) covers the operations of both the trading unit and the risk management unit. (c) The validation under (a) is capable of identifying the trading desks affected by a defect where there is a defect in the systems relating to market risk measurement. (d) The validation under (a) includes the following matters. (1) The appropriateness of the structure of the Market Risk Management Department. (2) The sufficiency of the documents on the theory of the risk management models and on model management procedures. (3) The accuracy and appropriateness of the risk management models. (4) The consistency, timeliness, reliability and independence of the input data used in the risk management models. (5) The appropriateness of the operating framework (including the valuation approval process) of the valuation models used by staff in the front office and the back office. (6) The appropriateness of the scope of market risk covered by the trading desk's risk management models. (7) The completeness of the management information system. (8) The accuracy and completeness of position data. (9) The accuracy and appropriateness of assumptions on volatility and correlation. (10) The accuracy of the methods of calculating valuations and risk amounts. (11) The appropriateness of the validation of the accuracy of the trading desk's risk management models through regular back-testing and profit-and-loss attribution tests. (12) The consistency between the model used to calculate the market risk equivalent amount and the internal management model.
